Definition: from Σήρ (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured; hence the name of the silk-worm); Seric, i.e. silken (neuter as noun, a silky fabric):--silk.
BiblicalUsage: Serikos is silk, and it stands in the merchandise of fallen Babylon: gold, and silver, and precious stones, and fine linen, and purple, and silk, and scarlet — the soft luxuries of a city about to fall. The Greek text behind the King James Version spells it with an eta, while the text I have checked spells it with an iota.
TheologicalSignificance: What I see here is that silk in Babylon's list is a luxury bought with souls — the merchants weep for it, and the city falls with it.
